Show or save the language-model settings

Source: R/llm_config.R
llmcfg.Rd

Every setting that decides how llmask reaches a model, in one place: which route to use; your key and model for each provider (bring your own key: see llmprvd); the address, key and model of your own OpenAI-compatible server; and of a local or LAN Ollama server. Called with no arguments it only reads: it returns a table of every setting, its current value, and where that value comes from. Called with key = value pairs it saves those settings first. Keys are never printed, only whether one is set.

Usage

llmcfg(...)

Arguments

...

Settings to save, as key = value. The keys are:

  • route: "auto", "own", "ollama" or a provider id such as "anthropic" (case is ignored);

  • <provider>.key and <provider>.model, for example anthropic.key or openai.model;

  • own.url, own.key and own.model;

  • ollama.url, ollama.model and ollama.key.

Each value is a single string (leading and trailing spaces are removed). NULL, NA or "" removes a saved setting. With no arguments nothing is written.

Value

A data frame with one row per setting (seven general settings followed by a key and a model row for each provider) and five character columns: key (the setting's name), value (its current value, the default spelled out; a key only as "set" or "(not set)"), source ("environment", "saved" or "default"), env (the environment variable that overrides it) and help (what it is for). Returned visibly when called with no settings, invisibly after saving.

Details

Where settings live. Saved settings are kept in llm.json in the folder $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/morie (~/.config/morie when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is unset), a private file (mode 0600, in a private directory) next to the shared credentials.json. The file is written only when you pass a setting; only the settings that change are rewritten in place, so the rest of the file stays exactly as it was. An empty set of settings removes the file.

Precedence. An environment variable that is set (the env column, for example ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OLLAMA_HOST) wins over a saved value, which wins over the built-in default. Saving a setting whose variable is set warns that the variable still wins. A provider key is also read from the provider's alternative variable where it has one: GOOGLE_API_KEY for Gemini, CO_API_KEY for Cohere, and for Hugging Face HUGGINGFACE_HUB_TOKEN.

Checks when saving. Names must be among the settings listed in the key column ("unknown setting" otherwise) and every value passed as key = value with one value each. route must be "auto", "own", "ollama" or a provider id; the retired "hosted" route is refused. own.url must be an http(s):// address and ollama.url an address or host:port; both are refused if they contain spaces, a fragment or user information, and, unless they point at this machine or a private LAN address, they get the package's public-address check (a metadata or link-local address is refused). "off", "none" or "disabled" turns a server off. A key with a line break or control character in it is refused. A new own.url or ollama.url drops the key saved for the old server (with a message), so a key is never sent to a server it was not saved for. A settings file that is not a JSON object, or holds a setting that is not a non-empty string, stops every call until it is fixed or moved aside with rmbl config reset.

Reading the settings takes a few milliseconds: the table of settings is built once per session and the file is read once per call. Nothing is sent over the network by this function.

The same is available from the shell: rmbl config lists the settings, rmbl config set KEY VALUE and rmbl config unset KEY change one (a key is asked for without echo when no value is given), and rmbl config setup walks through them.

See also

llmprvd for the providers and their variables, llmstat for which routes are reachable, llmask which uses these settings.

Examples

# Work in a temporary settings directory so your own settings are
# untouched.
old <- Sys.getenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", unset = NA)
Sys.setenv(XDG_CONFIG_HOME = tempfile("cfg"))

# Reading the settings writes nothing.
cfg <- llmcfg()
head(cfg[, c("key", "value", "source")])
#>            key                  value  source
#> 1        route                   auto default
#> 2      own.url              (not set) default
#> 3      own.key              (not set) default
#> 4    own.model              (not set) default
#> 5   ollama.url http://localhost:11434 default
#> 6 ollama.model (the first one pulled) default
nrow(cfg)
#> [1] 39

# Save a local Ollama model and use it for every request; the key column
# shows where each value now comes from.
llmcfg(ollama.model = "qwen3:8b", route = "ollama")
cfg <- llmcfg()
cfg[cfg$key %in% c("route", "ollama.model"), c("key", "value", "source")]
#>            key    value source
#> 1        route   ollama  saved
#> 6 ollama.model qwen3:8b  saved

# A key is shown only as set or not set.
llmcfg(own.url = "http://localhost:1234/v1", own.key = "k-123")
cfg <- llmcfg()
cfg$value[cfg$key == "own.key"]
#> [1] "set"

# Back to the defaults: NULL removes a saved setting.
llmcfg(route = NULL, ollama.model = NULL, own.url = NULL,
                      own.key = NULL)

# Unknown settings and retired routes are refused.
try(llmcfg(colour = "blue"))
#> Error : unknown setting 'colour' (one of: route, own.url, own.key, own.model, ollama.url, ollama.model, ollama.key, openai.key, openai.model, anthropic.key, anthropic.model, gemini.key, gemini.model, openrouter.key, openrouter.model, groq.key, groq.model, together.key, together.model, fireworks.key, fireworks.model, deepseek.key, deepseek.model, mistral.key, mistral.model, xai.key, xai.model, cerebras.key, cerebras.model, perplexity.key, perplexity.model, huggingface.key, huggingface.model, opencode.key, opencode.model, cohere.key, cohere.model, nvidia.key, nvidia.model)
try(llmcfg(route = "hosted"))
#> Error : the hosted MORIE language-model tier is retired: bring your own key (a provider's variable such as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY, or `rmoriebricklayer config set <provider>.key`) or run a model locally (Ollama); `rmoriebricklayer config setup` walks through it

if (is.na(old)) Sys.unsetenv("XDG_CONFIG_HOME") else Sys.setenv(XDG_CONFIG_HOME = old)
if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# your Anthropic key and model, and always use them
llmcfg(anthropic.key = "sk-ant-...", route = "anthropic")
# an Ollama server on another machine
llmcfg(ollama.url = "http://192.168.1.20:11434", ollama.model = "qwen3:8b")
}
